standard.title: Sequence collaborative production
standard.description: sequence steps to individually and collaboratively make designed solutions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can sequence steps for making designed solutions cooperatively (AC9TDE2P04). They have sequenced steps in a cooperative context. They have not yet worked with explicit planning tools (timelines, spreadsheets, flowcharts), managed time and resource allocation, or understood mass production processes.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students sequence steps to individually and collaboratively make designed solutions, using planning tools to record steps and manage time and resource allocation.

nodes.label: Planning and recording production steps
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can plan a production sequence and record it using a planning tool such as a timeline, list or flowchart
nodes.minimum_width: Record the steps for making a designed solution in sequence using at least one planning tool (e.g. a list, a timeline, a simple flowchart)
nodes.typical_width: Determine and record production steps using planning tools — timelines, spreadsheets, calendars or lists; include when parts of the project need to be completed; use planning tools for both individual and collaborative tasks
wider: Create a flowchart for a mass production process — for example, packing identical food boxes where each student has a separate task; identify decision points and parallel steps in the sequence

Draw a flowchart or record a video of a procedure with a fixed sequence (e.g. packing boxes for community members in need) — evaluate whether the recorded steps are clear and complete enough for someone else to follow

response_modes.reason: Students who only plan sequences for simple personal tasks may not understand how planning tools scale to more complex production. Experiencing planning for both individual making and multi-role collaborative production builds a more complete understanding of sequencing as a management tool.

success_criteria: Steps are recorded in a logical sequence using a planning tool
The sequence includes enough steps to complete the making task without missing key stages
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot record a production sequence cannot contribute to the role and resource allocation in N2 — planning tools are the shared artefact that makes role coordination possible.

nodes.label: Managing time and resource allocation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify roles and resources needed in a collaborative production task and explain how these are managed to complete the task
nodes.minimum_width: In a collaborative making task, identify at least two roles and the resources each role needs; contribute to a plan that allocates tasks
nodes.typical_width: Discuss the importance of managing time and resources throughout production; identify roles different people might take in a team; map tasks to roles and identify the resources each needs; contribute to a shared plan
wider: Plan a collaborative production event (e.g. food distribution for a community event) — identify all roles, resources and the sequence of tasks; discuss how delays or resource shortages in one role affect others
Reflect on a completed collaborative task — identify where time or resource management broke down and propose how the plan could be improved for next time

response_modes.reason: Resource and role allocation requires students to reason about dependencies — what does each person need, and what happens if a resource is unavailable? Scaffolding this reasoning (identify role → identify resource needed → identify what could block progress) builds production planning thinking rather than just task-listing.

success_criteria: Names at least two roles in a collaborative task
Identifies the resources each role needs to complete its tasks
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot reason about role dependencies and resource needs cannot coordinate a collaborative production in N3 — they will block other roles or run out of resources mid-task.

nodes.label: Individual and collaborative production sequences
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can sequence steps for both individual and collaborative production tasks and explain how collaborative sequences differ from individual ones
nodes.minimum_width: Complete a production task — individually or collaboratively — following a planned sequence, and describe at least one way the collaborative sequence required coordination that an individual sequence did not
nodes.typical_width: Sequence and follow production steps for both individual and collaborative tasks; explain how collaborative sequencing requires task allocation, timing coordination and role communication that individual sequencing does not; use a planning tool to manage the process
wider: Identify the steps in a mass production process — each student has a separate task in a production line (e.g. packing food boxes); discuss how the sequence must be coordinated so the whole production runs efficiently

Compare an individual production sequence with a collaborative one for the same product — identify which steps are divided, which are parallel and which must be sequential regardless of how many people are involved

response_modes.reason: This node integrates planning tools (node 1) with role and resource management (node 2) into a completed collaborative production experience. The integration challenge is coordinating steps, roles and resources simultaneously in real time — the coordination is the learning.

success_criteria: Follows a planned production sequence to completion
Describes at least one difference between individual and collaborative sequencing
